core_research_thesis: Designing an optimized battery through the integration of electrochemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, and thermodynamics to achieve high energy density, power density, and cycle life
state_of_the_art_prior_art: Lithium-ion batteries with graphite anodes and lithium cobalt oxide cathodes
Sodium-ion batteries with hard carbon anodes and prussian blue cathodes
Solid-state batteries with solid electrolytes and lithium metal anodes
proven_facts: The Nernst equation relates the electrode potential to the concentration of reactants and products
The Butler-Volmer equation describes the kinetics of electrochemical reactions
Fick's laws of diffusion govern the transport of ions and molecules in the electrolyte
Ohm's law relates the current and voltage in an electrical circuit
Thermodynamic laws govern the energy storage and conversion in batteries
critical_unanswered_unknowns: The optimal electrode material and design for high energy density and power density
The relationship between electrolyte composition and battery performance
The effects of temperature and pressure on battery performance and lifespan
The scalability and manufacturability of new battery technologies
The development of advanced battery management systems for optimal performance and safety

required_empirical_data_inputs: Electrode material properties (e.g. conductivity, porosity, surface area)
Electrolyte composition and properties (e.g. viscosity, conductivity, thermal stability)
Battery performance data (e.g. charge/discharge curves, capacity, energy density, power density)
Thermal and mechanical stress data (e.g. temperature, pressure, vibration)
Manufacturing and scalability data (e.g. production yields, defect rates, cost)
